🇺🇸🪖 With Gulf bases gone, US eyes foothold in the Horn of Africa
 
The US has taken a security interest in two of the UAE’s three illegal military bases in war-torn Somalia, making use of the facilities for troop transits and even setting up a limited special operations presence, NYT reports.
👉 The Berbera facility, situated in the Somaliland breakaway and built up and [expanded by the UAE](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/62031) over the past decade, was used twice by the US over the past year, according to flight tracking data, including to transit special operations commandos from Djibouti to Bosaso, Puntland for ‘counterterror cooperation’-related operations (at least two dozen US troops present).
The UAE’s network of bases in Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo (Jubaland) gives the Gulf sheikdom the ability to project power across east Africa in Somalia, Ethiopia and Sudan, and back to the Middle East (Houthi-controlled Yemen is as little as 300 km north of the Berbera base).
The US is “exploring using these bases as low-profile options” for its war with Iran, NYT said, citing US officials’ plans to “work with local partners in the region to defend US interests and provide…unique capabilities only the US has.”
👉 Somalia’s federal authorities, formally listed as a counterterrorism and maritime security partner to the US, protested the UAE’s construction of its [unauthorized bases ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78001)in breakaway areas this week. Earlier this year, Mogadishu formally cut off cooperation with the UAE and signed defense pacts with Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
UAE ‘Hexagon Alliance’ partner[ Israel ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76469)recognized Somaliland’s ‘independence’ last December, with the territory’s self-proclaimed president declaring readiness to both host foreign military forces and offer the US and its allies lucrative mineral and energy deals.

🚀 Houthis hammer Saudi power plant and port
Ansar Allah says it struck the Al-Shuqaiq power plant and Jazan port after [previously warning](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78058) that Saudi energy and port infrastructure would become targets if attacks on Yemen continued.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the operation came in response to Saudi strikes on power facilities in Saada and Mocha and the attack on Hodeidah port, Xinhua reported.
✅ Footage reportedly from Al-Shuqaiq shows a major fire and huge columns of smoke rising from the area.
Riyadh was quick to say that two ballistic missiles were intercepted over Jazan, with debris falling in Al-Shuqaiq.

events.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 Trump may be looking to wind down Iran conflict behind smokescreen of military options
The US seems to be scaling back its naval presence in the Arabian Sea, raising questions about President Donald Trump's alternative plans for the region.
👉 [The USS George Washington ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77978)aircraft carrier left the Middle East on November 18 after spending three months on station. It is returning to Yokosuka, Japan, with its strike group. Yokosuka is home to the US 7th Fleet. Previously, it had been deployed[ in the Arabian Sea](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77830) alongside the USS Theodore Roosevelt, which arrived in the region on November 15, and the USS George H.W. Bush, which arrived in April. Judging by the INSS interactive map, American warships are keeping their distance from the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf.
Reducing the US carrier presence in the region is an interesting choice after Washington assembled its largest naval force there since 2003, US analyst Brandon Weichert writes.
The departure of the USS George Washington also coincided with the APEC summit, where US President Donald Trump joined his Russian and Chinese counterparts at [the negotiating table](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78007.).
❗️Both Russia and China have long advocated a diplomatic solution to the Gulf crisis. At the summit, Trump signaled his interest in lasting peace in the region, prompting some observers to believe that he is considering "an alternative to massive escalation."
Meanwhile, US hawks and Israeli politicians are pressing him to resume the war with Iran. Last week in Washington, Gofman advocated joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran during meetings with CIA Director John Ratcliffe and US envoy Steve Witkoff.
👉 On November 18, US CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper held a trilateral meeting with IDF Chief of Staff Gen. Eyal Zamir and Mossad Director Roman Gofman in Tel Aviv to conduct an Iran threat assessment. On November 19, Axios reported that Trump had tasked the Pentagon and US intelligence agencies with assessing Iran’s possible responses to CENTCOM’s military strike scenarios.
Still, Weichert believes Trump is using security discussions as a smokescreen while scaling back the US naval presence and delaying any major escalation, largely due to depleted military stockpiles and incapability of decisively winning a war with Iran.
